questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord does not yet know of the defect (the tenant has not reported it and the landlord has not learned of it in another way)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord learned of the defect only orally, so that no written notice, written acknowledgement or inspection record of it exists?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the tenant claim compensation from the landlord for damage the defect caused to the tenant (for example damaged furniture or clothing, or extra costs)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that at least one rent payment has already been paid into deposit with the office designated by the canton?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant intends to pay the rent on deposit with the office designated by the canton instead of to the landlord, or has begun to do so?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?

text:
Hello,

My landlord, Birkenrain Property Ltd, has known about this for more than two months. I reported it to Mr Henry Palmer by e-mail on 20 January 2026, with photos, and the very next day he wrote back confirming he had received my message and would "organise someone". So there is no question of them not knowing.

It isn't just a matter of a phone call either. Apart from my e-mail and his written reply, Mr Palmer came to the flat on 3 February with a clipboard, looked at everything and gave me a copy of his inspection notes, signed by both of us.

I also want to be clear about what I am after. I'm not asking Birkenrain for any money for damage. Nothing of mine has been ruined and I haven't had any extra costs. I only want the problem fixed.

The problem is that the flat at Hofackerstrasse 59 in Lausanne is damp. Since early January the outside wall of the bedroom has been wet to the touch, the window frames drip with condensation every morning, and black mould has spread across the ceiling corner and behind the wardrobe. I air the room twice a day and keep the heating on, but the wall doesn't dry out. My partner Olivia Bachmann has asthma and has started sleeping on the sofa in the living room because the smell in the bedroom makes her cough. We pay CHF 2950 a month and effectively can't use one of our two bedrooms.

Since the inspection, nothing has happened. No workman, no date, no answer to my two follow-up e-mails. What can I do to get them to act?

Best regards,
Owen Hughes
